title: The Scholarship of Westbrook High
premise: Emrys Pemberton, Westbrook High's reigning debate champion, has perfected the art of being unnoticed — until her best friend Juniper vanishes, leaving behind a locker key that opens a hidden cache of evidence against the school board. Following Juniper's trail, Emrys uncovers a scheme to funnel scholarship funds to the board chair's cronies, with her own coveted full-ride as the prize being dangled to keep her quiet. As she balances the state debate championship with an underground investigation run by the school's misfits, she falls for Theo, the janitor's son whose father's testimony could destroy everything. In the end, Emrys wins the championship she no longer cares about, loses the scholarship on purpose by exposing the truth at the final awards assembly, and finds that Juniper — hiding in plain sight with an aunt two towns over — comes home to a family they built themselves.
about_author: Silas Sandoval is a former high school forensics coach who spent six years watching teenagers out-argue adults twice their age. He writes in a converted school bus outside Asheville, North Carolina, where he lives with two rescue dogs named after losing debate teams.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: Emrys Pemberton's POV. We meet her mid-debate, flawless in public and invisible at home, where her mother's new husband rules by silence. Establishes her survival strategy: never win an argument that matters. Emotional beat: the loneliness of being praised for compliance.

chapters.title: The Empty Desk
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Juniper doesn't show for their morning ritual, then doesn't show for three days. The school shrugs; the police file it under runaway. Emrys notices Juniper's locker cleaned out except one key taped inside the door. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Locker 114
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The key opens a storage room off the gym where Juniper kept a box: printouts of board meeting minutes, a burner phone, and a note reading 'If I'm gone, it's the scholarship list.' Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing your best friend was fighting a war alone.

chapters.title: The Misfit Table
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. She breaks her own rules and sits at the cafeteria's edge table — Theo the janitor's son, Priya the expelled-in-spirit hacker, and Marcus, who already knows too much about the board. Emotional beat: the terror and relief of being seen.

chapters.title: What the Money Buys
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya decrypts Juniper's files: scholarship funds redirected to board chair Alcott's contractors, with Emrys's name penciled in as the quiet recipient. Emotional beat: the sick discovery that your success was purchased to buy your silence.

chapters.title: Practice Round
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Her debate coach pushes her toward the state championship; her stepfather demands she quit 'distractions.' She rehearses arguments she doesn't believe while lying to everyone. Emotional beat: the gap between winning and being right.

chapters.title: Rooftop Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo tells Emrys his father signed a delivery receipt that could sink Alcott — and then lost his job for asking questions. On the roof, between almost-kisses, they agree the truth is worth more than safety. Emotional beat: love as a decision, not an accident.

chapters.title: The Burner Rings
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Juniper calls the burner for eleven seconds: 'Don't trust the counselor. I'm okay. Stop looking.' Then dead air. Priya traces the call to a town two hours away. Emotional beat: hope and suspicion wrestling in the dark.

chapters.title: Guidance
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Counselor Voss gently suggests Emrys drop the investigation, hinting the scholarship depends on being 'a team player.' Emrys plays dumb, records the conversation. Emotional beat: learning that kindness can be a leash.

chapters.title: State Semifinals
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. She wins her semifinal round on autopilot while Priya texts her Alcott's contractor invoices in real time. Marcus tails a board member to a storage unit. Emotional beat: the championship becoming a cover story for the real competition.

chapters.title: The Storage Unit
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus and Theo photograph boxes of falsified invoices, but a security guard — Alcott's cousin — catches them. They escape with the photos but Theo's father is summoned to the school the next morning. Emotional beat: the cost of evidence is always paid in people.

chapters.title: Detention
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Theo's father, threatened with deportation-adjacent pressure, recants. Theo, furious and ashamed, pushes Emrys away to protect her. She refuses to let him. Emotional beat: found family means you don't get to sacrifice yourself alone.

chapters.title: Juniper's Letters
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Among the locker contents, Emrys finally reads Juniper's unsent letters — about her mother's addiction, about being the one who always noticed everything, about trusting only Emrys. Emotional beat: grief for a friend who might still be alive.

chapters.title: The Trap She Left
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya realizes Juniper's files contain a dead man's switch: if Juniper misses a check-in, everything auto-sends to a journalist. It's set to fire in nine days — right before the championship. Emotional beat: realizing Juniper planned her own disappearance as a weapon.

chapters.title: Alcott's Offer
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Alcott corners Emrys: full ride, mother's debts cleared, in exchange for the burner phone. He mentions her stepfather's gambling markers. She says yes — and lies. Emotional beat: the moment invisibility becomes a weapon instead of a wound.

chapters.title: Two Towns Over
chapters.summary: Emrys and Theo's POV, alternating. They drive to the traced town and find Juniper alive, hiding with an aunt, too scared to come home. Juniper reveals the final piece: Alcott's signature page, the one document the dead man's switch doesn't have. Emotional beat: fury, relief, and the question of what justice requires.

chapters.title: The Argument at Home
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys finally wins the argument at home — telling her mother everything, refusing to be managed. Her mother wavers, then chooses her daughter, handing over proof of Alcott's pressure on the stepfather. Emotional beat: the first argument she's ever won, and it costs nothing but silence.

chapters.title: State Finals
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys debates the final round against a rival she once envied — and wins, decisively, arguing a case about complicity. The trophy means nothing now; the crowd means everything, because her misfits are in the front row. Emotional beat: winning the championship that doesn't matter, on her own terms.

chapters.title: The Final Audition
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. At the awards assembly, with Alcott beaming beside her, Emrys takes the microphone and instead of thanking the board, reads the invoices aloud, live-streamed by Priya. She forfeits the scholarship on stage. Emotional beat: the true final round, argued without a timer.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. Alcott resigns under investigation; the journalist's story breaks; the dead man's switch fires as backup. Theo's father gets his job back with back pay. The school tries to spin, and mostly fails. Emotional beat: justice outside the law is slow, messy, and real.

chapters.title: The Key We Keep
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Juniper comes home, moves in with Emrys's family for now, and the misfits claim Locker 114 as a monument — then empty it, because they don't need hiding places anymore. Emotional beat: found family formalized in borrowed space.

chapters.title: Debate Club, Renamed
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV, epilogue. Emrys starts an after-school club that teaches kids to argue with power, not just each other. She's lost the scholarship but earned a full-ride elsewhere — one she applied for herself. Final beat: she was never invisible; she was waiting.
